summary: Defines a Management Information Base (MIB) module for managing DS0 and DS0 bundle interfaces, the basic digital voice-grade channels used in telephone-style circuits. It lets network management tools using SNMP monitor and configure them. It is a companion to the MIB documents for DS1/E1 and DS3/E3 interfaces.

plainLanguage.summary: Phone companies carry calls in small digital lanes. This document gives a standard list of questions you can ask a device about those lanes, so one control program can check them on any brand of equipment.

subtitle: SNMP management objects for DS0 channels and the bundles of DS0s that carry faster data inside a DS1 or E1.

tldr.problem: Network management tools had no standard way to configure and monitor individual DS0 channels or groups of them, which are the basic units inside DS1 and E1 lines.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines two SMIv2 MIB modules. DS0-MIB describes each DS0 and maps channel numbers to interfaces. DS0BUNDLE-MIB lets a manager create bundles of DS0s and optionally describes BONDing for them.
tldr.outcome: Managers can read and set DS0 and DS0 bundle settings over SNMP in a uniform way, building on the interfaces MIB and its ifTable and ifStackTable.

facts.label: DS0s per DS1 in the example

today: RFC 2494 is a Proposed Standard published in January 1999. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: What the MIBs Cover
sections.content:
RFC 2494 defines part of the Management Information Base (MIB) used by network management protocols. It describes objects for managing DS0 and DS0 Bundle interfaces. It is a companion to the MIBs for DS1/E1/DS2/E2 (RFC 2495) and DS3/E3 (RFC 2496).

The objects apply to two values of ifType in the Internet-standard MIB: ds0 (81) and ds0Bundle (82). The memo specifies its MIB modules in a form that is compliant with the SNMPv2 SMI and semantically identical to the peer SNMPv1 definitions.

The document contains two modules. The DS0 MIB represents individual DS0s in a DS1 or E1. The DS0Bundle MIB represents collections of DS0s used together to carry data within a DS1/E1 at speeds greater than a single DS0. Bundles are created on top of DS0s and are shown that way in the ifStackTable.
sections.plainLanguage: A DS0 is one small lane on a phone line. A bundle is several lanes tied together to go faster. This document has one list of questions for lanes and one for bundles.

sections.title: How DS0s Use the Interfaces Table
sections.content:
DS0s and bundles appear as rows in the standard ifTable defined in RFC 2233. Only the ifGeneralInformationGroup and ifCounterDiscontinuityGroup need to be supported.

The RFC fixes several values. ifType is ds0(81) or ds0Bundle(82). ifSpeed is 64000 for a ds0, regardless of the setting of robbed bit signalling, or N*64000 for a ds0Bundle. ifPhysAddress holds the Circuit Identifier, or a zero-length octet string if none is assigned. ifLinkUpDownTrapEnable is set to disabled(2) with read-only access, ifHighSpeed is the rounded ifSpeed/1000000, and ifConnectorPresent is false(2).

The ifStackTable shows which interface sits on which. In the RFC's example, a Frame Relay service is carried on 4 ds0s of a ds1. The service sits above a ds0Bundle, the bundle sits above four ds0s, and each ds0 sits above the ds1. If the service uses a single ds0, the ds0Bundle is not required.
sections.plainLanguage: Every lane and every bundle gets a line in the equipment's big list of connections. A stack chart says which one sits on top of which, like a tower of blocks.

sections.title: The DS0 Configuration and Channel Mapping Tables
sections.content:
The DS0 Config Group is mandatory for all systems that use a DS0 interface. It has two tables. The dsx0ConfigTable has one entry for each DS0 interface, indexed by ifIndex. Its objects are:

  • dsx0Ds0ChannelNumber, the channel number of the ds0 on its DS1/E1 (0 to 31).
  • dsx0RobbedBitSignalling, whether Robbed Bit Signalling is on. It applies only to DS1 links; for E1 links it is always off.
  • dsx0CircuitIdentifier, the transmission vendor's circuit identifier, to help troubleshooting (up to 255 characters).
  • dsx0IdleCode and dsx0SeizedCode, the ABCD-bit codes sent when the ds0 is not connected or is connected and dsx0TransmitCodesEnable is enabled. dsx0ReceivedCode shows the code being received.
  • dsx0Ds0BundleMappedIfIndex, the ifIndex of the bundle the ds0 belongs to, or zero if none.

The dsx0ChanMappingTable maps a channel number on a channelized interface to the ifIndex of the individual ds0. The RFC notes that it gives the answer with a single lookup, instead of walking the ifStackTable.

In the channelization example, a DS3 with ifIndex 1 is channelized into 28 DS1s. When dsx1Channelization is set to enabledDs0, 24 DS0s are created for each DS1; setting it to disabled destroys them.
sections.plainLanguage: Each lane has a settings card: its lane number, a label for the wire, and some signal codes. A lookup table answers, which lane is number 5 on this line?

sections.title: Creating and Bonding DS0 Bundles
sections.content:
The DS0 Bundle Group is mandatory for systems that use a DS0Bundle interface. A manager creates a bundle by adding a row to dsx0BundleTable, which indirectly creates an ifTable row with ifType ds0Bundle(82). The row is indexed by dsx0BundleIndex, which is not the same as ifIndex, because the manager chooses the index of a creatable row while the agent selects ifIndex values. The agent reports its choice in dsx0BundleIfIndex.

To avoid races between managers, dsx0BundleNextIndex uses the TestAndIncr type. A manager reads it, writes the same value back, and if that fails because another manager used it, tries again. Then it sets dsx0BundleRowStatus to createAndGo. The RFC's compliance statement allows only active, createAndGo and destroy, because inactive rows in the bundle table do not make sense.

The DS0 Bonding Group is optional. dsx0BondMode says which BONDing mode a bundle uses: none(1), other(2), mode0(3), mode1(4), mode2(5) or mode3(6). Mode 0 gives parameter and number exchange with no synchronization. Mode 1 adds synchronization during initialization. Mode 2 adds inband monitoring and steals 1/64th of the bandwidth of each channel. Mode 3 also provides n x 56/64 kbit/s data channels. dsx0BondStatus reports idle(1), callSetup(2) or dataTransfer(3).
sections.plainLanguage: To make a bundle, you take a numbered ticket first so two managers do not grab the same number. Bonding is an extra set of rules for lanes that join together for a call.

sections.title: Worked ifIndex Examples
sections.content:
The RFC walks through bundle mapping. A DS1 with ifIndex 1 is channelized into 24 DS0s with ifIndex values 2 through 25. Two bundles are made on it: the first uses channels 1 and 2, the second channels 3 and 4. They get ifIndex values 26 and 27, and dsx0BundleTable has two entries (index 1 maps to 26, index 2 maps to 27).

In dsx0ConfigTable, ds0 channels 1 and 2 then point to 26 in dsx0Ds0BundleMappedIfIndex, channels 3 and 4 point to 27, and unbundled channels such as 5 and 6 show 0.
sections.plainLanguage: If four lanes are tied into two pairs, each lane's card says which pair it is in, and lanes not in any pair say zero.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC says SNMPv1 by itself is an insecure environment. Even on a secure network there is no control over who may read the objects. Implementors are advised to consider SNMPv3 security, specifically the User-based Security Model (RFC 2274) and the View-based Access Control Model (RFC 2275). It is the customer's responsibility to configure the SNMP entity so that only legitimate principals can reach these objects.

Setting some objects to an inappropriate value can cause loss of traffic: dsx0RobbedBitSignalling, dsx0IdleCode, dsx0SeizedCode, dsx0TransmitCodesEnable, dsx0BundleRowStatus, dsx0BondMode and dsx0BondRowStatus. Setting dsx0CircuitIdentifier or dsx0BundleNextIndex is described as mischievous but not harmful to traffic.
sections.plainLanguage: Some of these settings can cut off calls if set wrong, so only trusted people should be allowed to change them.
